newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour criticises water firms on high profits.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour criticises water firms on high profits.

text.p: The British main opposition Labour party said on Monday that it continued to consider new pricing rules for water companies which would set a "normal" level of profits with any excess reflected in price cuts.

"The extent of the price cuts could be related to a formula which shares out the excess profits between the utility and its customers," the party said in its annual report on the water industry, Floods of Cash, Floods of Excuses.'

Labour, which currently leads the ruling Conservative party in opinion polls with an election due within five months, said there would still be an incentive for efficiency because part of the excess would remain with the company.
Labour has long mulled this type of "sliding scale" regulation for the industry whereby a part of what it would deem to be excess profits would be given to consumers.
In the United States, a form of pure profit regulation has been accused by companies of eroding incentives for efficiencies.
Shares in water and sewerage companies showed little reaction to Labour's plans as these suggestions "have been swilling around for up to two years," one analyst said.
Severn Trent closed 2-1/2p pence higher at 683-1/2p while South West Water added just 1/2p to 588 pence.
"We have heard all these possibilities before and they are still just possibilities. If Labour comes out with a definitive policy on the profits, there might be more reaciton," the analyst said.
Labour has committed itself to introducing a one-off "windfall" tax on utility company profits if it wins power in a general election.
